title: European fans' knowledge of New Orleans jazz history
summary: Fans abroad know the old bands, photographs and books, and reminded him of forgotten New Orleans musicians; he mentions Henrik in Denmark.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah, well that's what they thought, but the most thing it was, I think it was because they said it was traditional. Yeah, they liked that. And they liked that, you see. And they really liked the band and all the fellas, they liked Jim, they liked everybody that was in the band. And everywhere we went at, we had a real welcome. And those fellas over there could tell me about musicians I didn't know anything about because they know that everybody played in Kit Thomas' band. And they called some fellas I didn't know. And they was telling me who was playing in bands years ago. They have all the pictures of all these bands that they have here. Every jazz book you can name, they have it. And they tell you all those things, and I say, well, it's a wonderful thing because I knew Buddy P.T., but I never did know, I think they say it's his father, somebody who played a trumpet, a trombone or something years ago. Joe P.T.
I didn't know him even, yeah.
Yeah, well, I was surprised. They had his picture there. And Buddy P.T., they knew all about Buddy P.T. and they have Mamie Smith. Oh, go ahead.
They knew something like Buddy P.T. and his stepfather and all?

Yeah, they know all those fellas and know all the members in Sam Morgan's band. And there was fellas that I had known very well and had forgot about and they were dead, you know? And I didn't think about it. And they called their names and it brought back memories. And we met a fella over there called Henrik in Denmark who traveled with the band and he was one of the swellest fellas you ever want to meet. Did bother you going down the wrong side of the street?
